columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Primarily used by influencers, content creators, and course creators monetizing Instagram, TikTok, and other social platforms.
Free tier: unlimited free plan for a custom bio link on a hy.page URL.
Pro ≈USD 19/month, sell products, accept donations, take fan requests, remove HYpage branding.
Enterprise ≈USD 39/month, sell subscriptions/memberships (Patreon-style) embedded in the bio link.

strengths.title: Monetization-focused bio link
strengths.detail: Goes beyond standard link-in-bio, a micro membership/storefront to sell merch, subscriptions, digital products, and premium content.

strengths.title: Multiple revenue streams in one page
strengths.detail: Premium videos, files, ebooks, downloads, memberships, donations, and custom fan requests (shoutouts, custom videos).

strengths.title: Built-in payment processing
strengths.detail: Integrated Stripe and PayPal checkout; file delivery, payment security, and access handled by HYpage.

strengths.title: Funnel and upsell tools
strengths.detail: Sales funnels, order bumps, templated storefronts with after-purchase upsells, coupons, and multiple pricing options.

weaknesses.title: Higher pricing vs some alternatives
weaknesses.detail: Pro ≈USD 19/month and Enterprise ≈USD 39/month can feel steep for beginners vs Linktree Pro (~USD 6–9/month).

weaknesses.title: Limited payment gateways
weaknesses.detail: Only Stripe and PayPal, no local payment methods or alternative processors in some regions.

weaknesses.title: Freemium paywall on advanced features
weaknesses.detail: Generous free tier, but products, donations, subscriptions, and branding removal need Pro or Enterprise.

weaknesses.title: Smaller ecosystem vs Linktree/Beacons
weaknesses.detail: Less widely known; fewer integrations and martech options than bigger link-in-bio competitors.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Hypage is link-in-bio, landing pages, or creator storefronts. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Hypage is a cloud-based link management platform that lets creators sell work directly and manage social presence in one place, a customizable bio landing page for Instagram/TikTok to generate revenue, including exclusive content, memberships, donations, and custom requests.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Hypage side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Hypage you can use Memberships and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. You only need a door: route followers to many tools, or a thin storefront you already know.

Using Kahana with Hypage

You can use both. Hypage keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep Hypage as the door that routes followers to many tools. Add Kahana as what they open: a profile and hubs, listed on Explore, with optional paywalls. Put Kahana as the main learn or buy link on Hypage so the bio is not twelve exits and no room behind them.
